headline: Manus, the AI agent start-up that Meta tried to buy, has raised more than $500 million in its first funding round since the sale was undone.
score_reason: Large round for a company at the centre of a blocked US-China deal; announced by the company and confirmed across outlets.
importance_line: What changed is that a company whose sale to Meta was blocked by Chinese authorities has found new funding at home, which matters to the people and businesses using Manus agents, software that does tasks such as research with little human input, then to investors in Chinese AI, and the doubt is the undisclosed valuation and whether a reported Hong Kong listing plan goes ahead.
summary: TechCrunch reports that Butterfly Effect, the parent company of Manus, said in a WeChat post that it has raised more than $500 million, led by Boyu Capital and IDG Capital with Tencent, HSG and ZhenFund also taking part. It is the first round since Chinese authorities ordered Meta's $2 billion-plus purchase unwound in April 2026; no valuation was disclosed, though Manus was said last month to be in talks at about $4 billion.
notes: Pool item came from Reuters (blocked, 401); the same announcement was read at TechCrunch and credited to it. Cross-checked with The Next Web.
